newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish National Lottery raises 101.2mln punts in 96.
newsitem.headline: Irish National Lottery raises 101.2mln punts in 96.

text.p: The Irish National Lottery said on Thursday that it raised a record 101.2 million Irish pounds for beneficiaries in 1996.
Total sales for the year rose by five million to 308 million Irish pounds and players won 158 million in prizes.
"The growth in sales came from the Lotto side of the business and was largely due to two quite exceptional roll-over sequences toward the end of the year," the National Lottery said in a statement.
The total return to the community was 259.3 million or 84.2 percent of sales. Operating costs were 49 million or 15.8 percent of sales.
John Hynes, chairman of the lottery, said the overall growth in sales was the lowest ever recorded by the National Lottery and was indicative of a fiercely competitive Irish gaming market.

"The vigour and diversity of that market is a recent phenomenon featuring real competition from the UK National Lottery and the heavy involvement of licensed bookmakers in bets on the results of our Lotto draw," he said.
But the lottery said it was well positioned to respond to the challenges of the marketplace with whatever innovation was required.
